description: A gravelled precinct opposite a Roman theatre in Canterbury, the precinct has been known about since at least 1970, and temples are assumed to have been present. So far the only certain temple that has been identified is a Romano-Celtic temple in the western most corner of the precinct, first discovered in 1976. The dating evidence is not ideal but a construction date 100-120 CE and a demolition date of 350-360 CE has been put forward. Further to the east masonry walls have been observed, which have been suggested to be part of an expected monumental classical temple, but this is too tentative to entertain at this point.
